Catering and large orders need at least two weeks of lead time, and weekends fill up fast in graduation season.

If you are picking up individual items instead of booking a package, keep the table simple. Two or three items are enough for most parties. Brownie cookies give you texture. Chocolate chip cookies give you a familiar favorite. Mini banana bread or mini cake loaves give the table height and variety. A table with four trays of the same cookie looks boring. A table with three distinct items looks curated.

Choosing a Theme and Color Palette for Your Dessert Table

Your dessert table should match the graduate's school colors or party theme. The easiest way to do that is through napkins, signage, table runners, and serving trays, not through artificial food coloring on every dessert. The baked goods themselves can stay natural and simple. The surrounding decor carries the color.

Graduation tables tend to use school colors aggressively. That is fine, but the table reads better in photos when one neutral color breaks it up. A wooden board, a white platter, or kraft paper packaging can do that. Cookie party favor bags from Kassey's Kitchen already use kraft bags with ribbon and a custom tag. If you order favor bags for a graduation party, you can put the graduate's name, graduation year, or a short message on the tag. Cookie party favor bags are $5.50 per bag. The minimum is 20 bags, and each bag holds two cookies.

For the table itself, pick one focal point. A small chalkboard or printed sign near the center works better than banners hanging behind the table. Custom signage comes with the catering packages, which takes one task off your list. If you are handling decor yourself, put the sign at eye level and keep the wording short: the graduate's name and year is enough.

Must-Have Desserts for a Graduation Dessert Table

A graduation dessert table needs items that people can grab and eat while standing. That means no plates, no forks, no cutting, and no melting. The best fit from the Kassey's Kitchen menu is the cookie and mini loaf family.

Brownie cookies are a strong anchor for a graduation table. They are rich and fudgy with crisp edges and gooey centers. They feel more special than a standard brownie because the texture is somewhere between a brownie and a cookie. Brownie cookies are $5 for two.

Chocolate chip cookies are the reliable pick. They are thick, chewy, and loaded with semi-sweet chocolate chips. Every party has a few guests who want the familiar option, and this is it. Chocolate chip cookies are $5 for two.

Mini banana bread loaves add a different shape and a softer flavor. Mini banana bread is $5 each. The mini size is useful because guests can take one whole without feeling like they committed to a large slice. A large banana bread loaf is $25 if you prefer to slice and arrange the bread yourself on a tray.

Chocolate conchas are a Mexican bakery classic with a chocolate twist. The soft sweet bread has a crispy chocolate shell on top. They photograph beautifully and work well on a table with a graduation theme that leans into cultural traditions. Chocolate conchas are $5 each.

Mini cake loaves are $5 each. Flavors vary, so you will need to ask Kassey what is available around your party date. They give the table a cake presence in small, handheld form.

The best combination for a table is usually a cookie, a second cookie or concha, and a mini loaf or cake loaf. That gives you crunch, chew, softness, and visual height.

Budget-Friendly Graduation Dessert Table Planning Tips

The fastest way to overspend on a dessert table is to buy too many different items. Every extra variety means another tray, another price point, and more leftovers. A controlled table with three items often looks better and costs less than a sprawling table with six.

Start with pricing that fits your guest count. Brownie cookies and chocolate chip cookies are $5 for two. Mini banana bread, chocolate conchas, and mini cake loaves are $5 each. If you have 20 to 40 guests, a short list of three items such as one cookie option, one mini loaf option, and one concha option is a simple budget worksheet. For example, you might plan a pickup order with brownie cookies, mini banana bread, and chocolate conchas. List the number of each item in your request and Kassey will confirm details and pricing within 24 to 48 hours.

If you want grab-and-go favors instead of an open table, cookie party favor bags cost $5.50 per bag with a minimum of 20 bags, which gives guests a small, tidy package with custom tags.

For a hosted dessert table at a 20 to 40 guest graduation party, the Sweet Treat Table starts at $250. That includes the spread, cookie assortment, styling, and signage. For 50 or more guests, full dessert catering is custom quoted. Request a quote early and ask what fits your budget rather than guessing.

One more budget tip: do not double up on dessert if you are also serving another dessert from a family member. One strong dessert table is enough. If a relative insists on bringing a dessert, build your table around smaller handheld items so the two desserts do not compete.

Setup and Display Ideas That Photograph Well

Graduation dessert tables get photographed more than they get eaten in the first hour. People take pictures before they take a cookie. That means your display matters as much as your menu.

Use height. Put mini cake loaves and mini banana breads on a small riser, a wooden crate, or a stack of books covered with a cloth. Flat trays of cookies sit in front. Conchas look best grouped on a round platter or cake stand. The height difference makes the table look fuller without adding more desserts.

Keep labels short. A small card that says "brownie cookies" or "chocolate conchas" is enough. Do not clutter the table with long descriptions. Custom signage is included; ask Kassey whether individual dessert labels are included.

Think about timing. Set the table up close to dessert time. That keeps the cookies and breads from sitting out too long. For pickup orders, keep everything in sealed containers until setup time.

Leave room for napkins and small plates if you serve the large banana bread loaf sliced. A stack of cocktail napkins near the table edge is enough for cookies and minis. Do not crowd the center with napkins; put them on one side.

For favor bags, line them up in rows on a side table rather than the main dessert table. The kraft bags with ribbon and custom tags will look like part of the decor, and guests can take one on the way out.

Published October 23, 2026

Before you plan a dessert table for a birthday, office party, or graduation, what to ask a home baker before ordering event desserts can save you from missed deadlines, unclear pickup details, and allergy surprises. Every item is handmade from scratch with no shortcuts, no mixes, and no freezer. When you send a request through the order form, you are not placing a confirmed order. You are opening a conversation about your date, guest count, menu choices, and event logistics.

What to ask a home baker before ordering event desserts

Most event dessert problems happen before baking starts. A host forgets to ask about lead time and sends a request too late. Another assumes delivery is included and only finds out later that individual orders are pickup only. A third does not mention a tree nut allergy until after the menu is set. Kassey's Kitchen works in small batches and bakes fresh for your date, so the details you share in a request shape what she can do.

Asking clear questions also saves time on both sides. Kassey replies within 24 to 48 hours to confirm details, pricing and the date. Include your event date, guest count, menu choices, and allergy notes in your request. The more specific you are about your event, the fewer follow-up messages you need before you know what is possible.

Kassey caters desserts for birthday parties, baby showers, bridal showers, quinceañeras, corporate events, graduation parties, weddings and holiday parties. The same set of questions applies whether you need a small pickup order or a full dessert table.

Ask about lead time and order deadlines

Lead time is one of the first things to confirm. Regular orders need at least 3 to 5 days. Catering and large orders need at least 2 weeks. Weekends fill up fast, so a Saturday event needs a request earlier than a last minute text. Kassey replies within 24 to 48 hours to confirm details, pricing and the date. That reply matters because your initial request is not a confirmed order.

If you are planning a graduation party, look at planning a dessert table for a graduation party for layout ideas. Then send a request with your event date and guest count. For example, a graduation party within the 20 to 40 guest range may fit the Sweet Treat Table package. Because that is catering, send the request at least 2 weeks before the event, not a few days before.

A regular order is simpler. If you want brownie cookies and mini banana bread for a small gathering, give Kassey at least 3 to 5 days. Mention the planned pickup date in your request so she can tell you whether the date is still open.

Ask about customization and menu options

The core menu is small and specific. Brownie cookies and chocolate chip cookies are $5 for 2. Mini banana bread, chocolate conchas, and mini cake loaves are $5 each. A large banana bread loaf is $25.

Brownie cookies are rich, fudgy brownie-meets-cookie with crisp edges and gooey centers. Chocolate chip cookies are thick, chewy, and loaded with semi-sweet chocolate chips and a hint of vanilla. Chocolate conchas are a Mexican bakery classic with a chocolate twist, soft sweet bread topped with a crispy chocolate shell.

Cookie Party Favor Bags: $5.50 per bag, 2 cookies per bag, kraft bag with ribbon, custom tag with your message, minimum 20 bags.

Catering packages are fully customizable starting points. You can ask for a combination of brownie cookies, chocolate chip cookies, chocolate conchas, or mini banana bread. Ask about allergen handling and cross-contact

Ask about allergies before you get attached to a menu. Everything at Kassey's Kitchen is made in a home kitchen that handles nuts, dairy, wheat and eggs. Because of that, allergen-free products cannot be guaranteed. If you have a guest with a serious nut allergy or dairy restriction, say so in your order request. The kitchen handles nuts, dairy, wheat and eggs, and allergen-free products cannot be guaranteed. Do not assume that removing an ingredient makes an item safe from cross-contact.

This is not the place to expect a guarantee that a dessert is free of nuts, dairy, wheat, or eggs. The honest answer is that the kitchen handles those common allergens. Ask the question, state the allergy clearly, and let the baker tell you what is possible. Mention allergies early because it may change which menu items fit your event.

Ask about pickup, delivery, and setup

Do not assume every event dessert order includes delivery. Individual orders at Kassey's Kitchen are pickup only. Pickup details are confirmed with your order.

Catering orders can include delivery for an additional fee. The fee may depend on distance. Full Dessert Catering for 50+ guests includes delivery, setup, table setup and styling, and custom signage. If you need a dessert table dropped off and arranged at a venue, ask for a full catering quote rather than ordering individual items and expecting setup.

For a smaller event, ask whether delivery is available and what it costs before you finalize your request. This is especially important for a shower or office event in a rented space, because you may need time to coordinate with a venue.

Ask about pricing, deposits, and payment methods

Get a clear price list in writing. Core individual prices are simple: brownie cookies and chocolate chip cookies are $5 for 2. Mini banana bread, chocolate conchas, and mini cake loaves are $5 each. A large banana bread loaf is $25. Cookie party favor bags are $5.50 per bag with a minimum of 20 bags. The Sweet Treat Table starts at $250. Full Dessert Catering is a custom quote for 50+ guests.

Payment methods Kassey accepts are Venmo, Zelle, Apple Cash, Cash App, PayPal, or cash. For custom or catering orders, a deposit may be required. Catering deposits secure the date, and full payment is due 3 days before the event. Ask what the deposit amount is when you submit your request, and ask for the deadline in writing.
